html:
The Willapa, or Kwalhioqua, were a small Athabaskan people of the Willapa Hills and the upper Willapa and Chehalis rivers in southwestern Washington. They were among the most isolated Athabaskan speakers, far south of the main Dene lands, and they shared their language with the Clatskanie across the Columbia.

They lived as hunters in the wooded hills, while the coast and rivers below were held by the Chinook and the Salishan Chehalis. Epidemics in the early 1800s struck them hard, and by the 1850s only a handful remained; they merged with the Chehalis and the Cowlitz. Their language has long been extinct.
